ai.title: encryptedapikeys table and AES-256-GCM crypto utilities
ai.summary: Added `encrypted_api_keys` table to the database schema to store user API keys securely. Introduced `common/src/api-keys/crypto.ts` providing AES-256-GCM encryption/decryption functions requiring a 32-byte `API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_SECRET`. The schema defines an `api_key_type` enum (`anthropic`, `gemini`, `openai`) with a composite primary key on `user_id` and `type`. Migration `0012_fluffy_naoko` applies the new table and foreign key constraint to the `user` table.

eli5.text: The app can now remember your secret login tokens for other AI services securely, instead of keeping them lying around unlocked. A new locked storage box was added to the database, where your tokens are scrambled with military-grade encryption that only your account can unscramble. If you signed in and connected an AI service like Google's Gemini, your token would now be tucked away safely in this encrypted box rather than stored in plain sight. This protection is active today for anyone using the newer features.

ai.title: Web UI refresh: neo-brutalist buttons, green theme, favicon fix
ai.summary: Website UI updated to neo-brutalist style. Pricing and navbar buttons now use `DecorativeBlocks` with `framer-motion` hover effects and white/black contrast instead of blue/purple gradients. Referral and pricing cards switched to green/emerald gradient palettes. Favicon path corrected to `favicon-32x32.ico` in `layout.tsx`. Hero text capitalized in `page.tsx`.

eli5.text: The website's buttons and overall look changed to a bold, high-contrast style: pricing and login buttons now have a stark black-and-white appearance with a slight shadow effect instead of the old blue and purple gradients. The referral and pricing pages switched to green-themed gradients for their cards. The browser tab icon (favicon) now displays correctly, and the main headline on the homepage ('Direct your codebase like a movie') was capitalized. You would notice these changes immediately if you visited the pricing, login, or referral pages.

ai.title: Affiliates page, handle column, referral limit 500
ai.summary: New /affiliates page lets users set unique handles via web/src/app/affiliates/actions.ts, raising referral_limit to 500 (AFFILIATE_USER_REFFERAL_LIMIT). DB migration 0013 adds user.handle text column with UNIQUE constraint. CREDITS_REFERRAL_BONUS drops 500 to 250 in common/src/constants.ts. /{sponsee} route now queries db by handle instead of static sponseeConfig map.

eli5.text: The affiliate program now lets each participant claim a custom username and raise their referral cap from the old default to 500 friends they can recruit. Your referral page address changes from a fixed system name to whatever username you pick, and the credit reward per new referral is halved from 500 to 250 points. If you're already signed up through an existing program link, your old address still works, but new links must use the new usernames. The higher 500-referee limit is live right away for anyone who fills out the new affiliate settings page.

ai.title: Undo smart redirect logic in NextAuth
ai.summary: Reverted complex redirect handling in `web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/auth-options.ts` to a simpler query-param-based redirect to `/onboard`. Removed `logger` dependency and associated logging statements. Simplified `web/src/components/sign-in/sign-in-button.tsx` by removing client-side `callbackUrl` construction and `usePathname`/`useSearchParams` hooks, relying on default `signIn` behavior.

eli5.text: When you sign in to the app, you'll now be sent to a simpler, more predictable landing page after logging in. The system used to try to guess the best place to send you based on extra details in the login link, but it sometimes sent you to the wrong spot or behaved unexpectedly. The app now ignores those extra details and always takes you to the onboarding screen, which is where most new users need to go. This makes the sign-in flow more reliable and easier to debug if something goes wrong.

ai.title: Add encrypted API key storage and Gemini client support
ai.summary: New `common/src/api-keys` module introduces AES-256-GCM encryption for Anthropic, Gemini, and OpenAI keys, with `retrieveAndDecryptApiKey` exported for backend use. `backend/src/llm-apis/gemini-api.ts` now accepts an optional `apiKey` parameter, instantiating per-key OpenAI clients while retaining a shared instance for the internal `GEMINI_API_KEY`. `main-prompt.ts` switches to `streamGemini25ProWithFallbacks` and filters `<codebuff_rate_limit_info>` and `<codebuff_no_user_key_info>` tags from the final response string. A new `web/src/app/api/api-keys/route.ts` endpoint exposes key management to the frontend.

eli5.text: The assistant can now connect to Google's Gemini AI models, not just Anthropic and OpenAI. Your personal API keys for these services are now stored encrypted and protected, so the system keeps them safer than before. If you provide a Gemini key, the assistant uses your key first, then falls back to others if needed. This is live today for anyone supplying their own API key.

ai.title: Smart redirecting fix attempt
ai.summary: Updated redirect logic in `web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/auth-options.ts` to distinguish between CLI and Web auth flows. If an `auth_code` query param is present, it redirects to `/onboard` preserving all params; otherwise, it allows relative or same-origin URLs to pass through, defaulting to `baseUrl` for external/invalid targets. Added `logger` import to track these routing decisions.

eli5.text: If you're logging in through the command-line tool, you're now sent to the onboarding page with all your login details safely attached, instead of ending up somewhere unexpected. If you're logging in through the website, you'll only be redirected to other website pages or verified addresses, and anything questionable bounces you back to the main page. The system now quietly notes where everyone gets sent, so the team can spot problems faster. This is live today.
